brief: D-060 reopened with corrections (brief-js161-reopen.md): the roles, e2e and differential stacks declared transcodeCores only because JS-161's build added it; the dogfood declares 3, so holding JS-161 changes nothing there; the suite itself meets the gap (queue run 45135324010, 9 cmd/jellyscale tests). Measured with 4 test processes on 4 pinned CPUs: an undeclared worker's speed 0.174 to 0.732 (capacity 0.70 to 2.93 on 4 processors), a 720p re-encode refused as 'cores are short' until the next start; a worker registering 5.3 s after start and the waiting request refused at 6.0 s; the benchmark beside live jobs timing out or reading 0.105 to 0.109 while those jobs ran at 0.586x and 0.95x. Options: A hold JS-161 for a redesign, B merge without the start-up measurement, C change what is measured then merge, D amend the 9 checks.
tradeoff: Given up, by operators who declare nothing on a CPU slower per core than the reference machine or on SMT threads, and by their viewers: the refusal with a reason for a play that worker cannot hold; it is admitted and stalls, as on main, with the operator told once in the log and on /metrics. D-044's 'capacity is measured on the worker at start, not declared' is set aside until a measurement exists that a busy host does not move and that slows no film. The dogfood declares its capacity and is unaffected. No viewer loses anything main gives.
entry: Option B. JS-161 merges without any benchmark, at start or beside work: an undeclared worker counts each processor at the reference speed with no floor, registers at once, and says in its log and on /metrics that its capacity is assumed; transcodeCores is the way to be exact, and docs/running.md says when an undeclared worker overstates itself and how to choose the figure. JS-161 criterion 2 is replaced, 3, 5 and 9 read 'declared' for 'measured', 7 names transcodeCores on an assumed worker, and a new criterion 12 returns the roles, e2e and differential stacks to undeclared workers and requires the 9 failed tests to pass unamended; one that still fails returns as a brief. D-060 is superseded: its gap never ships and its Changed guarantees and docs lines are removed. JS-176 is dropped and JS-166 no longer depends on it; JS-166 criterion 9 records declared capacity against job speeds. Of D-061: JS-176 criterion 5 is void (its substance is JS-161 criterion 2), JS-161's build is next with JS-174 beside it, BL-257 closes, and the i5-6500's 2.7 stays marked computed. BL-252 closes into BL-259 (an undeclared slow or SMT worker counts more than it holds), which carries what a measurement must meet: no delay to registration, no film slowed, a figure a busy host does not move, shown on a 4-process run. Rejected: D (the suite would stop showing measured viewer losses, and two of the checks guard existing guarantees), C (an unpriced redesign with unverified leaves ahead of JS-166), A (holds JS-166 for a capability the merge does not need). Reopens on: the assumed-capacity slow reason counted on any deployment; JS-166 showing a declared figure wrong by more than a fifth; JS-056 starting; any of the 9 tests failing after the measurement is out.
serves: PRODUCT.md: 'Nothing breaks the viewers' evening. Upgrades, a lost machine and a database failover happen without interrupting anyone.'; 'every failure is reported with its reason, never silent'; 'configuration is declarative'. Owner, 2026-11-22: nothing outruns the product.
